sections.title: 88-93 Behavior of the unbelievers with Prophet Shu'aib

translation.text: The arrogant chiefs of his people threatened, “O Shu’aib! We will certainly expel you and your fellow believers from our land, unless you return to our faith.” He replied, “Even if we hate it?
The disbelieving chiefs of his people threatened, “If you follow Shu’aib, you will surely be losers!”
Then an ˹overwhelming˺ earthquake struck them and they fell lifeless in their homes.

commentary.text: Those who rejected Shu’aib were ˹wiped out˺ as if they had never lived there. Those who rejected Shu’aib were the true losers.
Their punishment of came in the form of a violent earthquake.

Lesson: It is mostly the elite who oppose the message of Allah SWT because they suffer the consequences of equality and fairness for all thus diminishing their domination of power and their way of life (that often contradicts the Quran). The majority or the masses just follow along unquestioning and subservient.

sections.title: 94-99 Adversity and affluence are reminders from Allah

intro.text: After narrating individually, the stories of how various nations responded to the Message of their Prophets, the Quran now spells out the general rule which has been operative throughout the ages.

First, before the appearance of a Prophet the nations concerned were subject to a variety of afflictions and punishments such as famine, epidemics, colossal losses in trade and business, defeat in war etc. Such events make people conducive to heed the words of warning and turn to God in humility.

But if the people continue to refrain from embracing the truth they are subjected to another kind of test - that of affluence. This last test signals the beginning of their destruction. Forgetting Allah SWT and never showing any gratitude for the abundant wealth and luxury is before they are subject to huge destruction.
This is the sunnah of Allah SWT.
Lesson: Allah SWT does not punish immediately. First there are hardships and suffering, then ease, then sudden and devastating punishment.

Never fear that Iman will lead to poverty or deprivation rather Allah SWT provides blessings to His believers whether it be in the form of peace and contentment, worldly wealth or in some other way. Allah SWT gives His believing servants a good life.
Principle to live by is when you first hear then obey immediately otherwise you get desensitized after hearing the command the 50th time and do not obey.

sections.title: 100-102 Stories of prior nations are narrated to teach a lesson

translation.text: We have narrated to you ˹O Prophet˺ some of the stories of those societies. Surely, their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but still they would not believe in what they had already denied. This is how Allah seals the hearts of the disbelievers.

commentary.text: Hazrat Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shuaib have all been mentioned to teach a lesson but only for those who believe.

sections.title: 103-108 Prophet Moses was sent for the guidance of Pharaoh and his chiefs

translation.text: Then after them We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they wrongfully rejected them. See what was the end of the corruptors!
Moses said, ‘Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of all the Worlds,
Duty-bound to say nothing about God but the truth, and I have brought you a clear sign from your Lord. Let the Children of Israel go with me.’
Pharaoh said, “If you have come with a sign, then bring it if what you say is true.”
So Moses threw down his staff and—behold!—it became a real snake.
Then he drew his hand ˹out of his collar˺ and it was ˹shining˺ white for all to see.
The chiefs of Pharaoh’s people said, “He is indeed a skilled magician,

commentary.text: Now is the Story of Prophet Musa (PBUH)

Musa (PBUH) was sent to Pharaoh to invite him to two things; first, to surrender himself to God (i.e. Islam); and second, to release the Israelites - who were already Muslims - from his oppressive bondage.
Musa (PBUH) was granted two miraculous signs in order to provide testimony to his being a Messenger of God. The miracle of the staff and his hand.

The fact that Musa (PBUH)’s claim to prophethood implied total change including political change. For if a person lays claim to be God's Messenger, it implies that people obey him unreservedly. For God's Messengers are not sent to the world to obey other human beings and live in subordination to them; they rather ask others to accept them as their leaders and rulers. It is this which explains why Pharaoh and his coterie felt threatened by an all-out revolution -political, economic and social - when Musa (PBUH) came forth with his call.
Hence, they dubbed Moses a sorcerer so as to refute his claim to prophethood.

sections.title: 109-126 Moses' confrontation with the magicians of Pharaoh

translation.text: Then We inspired Moses, “Throw down your staff,” and—behold!—it devoured the objects of their illusion!
So the truth prevailed and their illusions failed.
And the magicians fell down, prostrating.
They declared, “We ˹now˺ believe in the Lord of all worlds—
Pharaoh threatened, “How dare you believe in him before I give you permission? This must be a conspiracy you devised in the city to drive out its people, but soon you will see.
I will certainly cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, then crucify you all.”
Your rage towards us is only because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Our Lord! Shower us with perseverance, and let us die while submitting ˹to You˺.”

commentary.text: The magicians instantly recognized that Musa (PBUH) was not a magician. They immediately accepted! And bowed down in prostration to Allah SWT.
Pharaoh was enraged as he was publicly humiliated and made to look weak Infront of his nation. He threated to crucify the magicians.

But once Iman entered the heart of the magicians there was no turning back. They were prepared to die but only die in the state of Iman. The dua of the magicians is asking for steadfastness and to die in a state of submission to Allah SWT.

sections.title: 127-129 Pharaoh's revenge against the people of Moses

translation.text: The chiefs of Pharaoh’s people protested, “Are you going to leave Moses and his people free to spread corruption in the land and abandon you and your gods?” He responded, “We will kill their sons and keep their women. We will completely dominate them.”

Moses reassured his people, “Seek Allah’s help and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah ˹alone˺. He grants it to whoever He chooses of His servants. The ultimate outcome belongs ˹only˺ to the righteous.”

commentary.text: Pharaoh had the baby boys of BI killed at birth but kept baby girls alive so as to gain domination over the Bani Israel.
Advice of Musa (PBUH) at the is time of huge difficulty for his nation was (i) to seek Allah SWT’s help and (ii) to be patient. And know that the ultimate victory is with the Believers.

Lesson: At times of extreme pain this is the formula for success. Seek Allah SWT help via zikr, dua, and understanding that only Allah SWT can aid us and being steadfast in our Iman. Aversity should strengthen our love and connection with Allah SWT.

sections.title: 130-137 Scourge of Allah against Pharaoh and his chiefs, and their final destruction

translation.text: Indeed, We afflicted Pharaoh’s people with famine and shortage of crops so they might come back ˹to their senses˺.
So We plagued them with floods, locusts, lice, frogs, and blood—all as clear signs, but they persisted in arrogance and were a wicked people.
But as soon as We removed the torment from them—until they met their inevitable fate—they broke their promise.
And so, because they rejected Our signs and paid them no heed, We exacted retribution from them: We drowned them in the sea

commentary.text: Allah SWT seized Pharaoh and his nation with famine, floods, locust, lice, frog and blood yet they remained arrogant. After each punishment was averted via the help and prayers of Musa (PBUH) they would revert back to their wrong ways.
So Allah SWT drowned them. The sea parted for Musa (PBUH) and the people of Bani Israel but Pharaoh and his followers were drowned. This punishment came suddenly, unexpectedly and with a vengeance.
Lesson: Through hard times Allah SWT is always teaching us. Be insightful enough to try and understand.

sections.title: 138-141 Allah rescued the Children of Israel but they still disbelieved in One God

translation.text: And We made those who had been oppressed succeed to both the east and the west of the land that We had blessed. Your Lord’s good promise to the Children of Israel was fulfilled, because of their patience, and We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people were making and what they were building.

commentary.text: The Israelites were made the inheritors of Palestine.

translation.text: We brought the Children of Israel across the sea and they came upon a people devoted to idols. They demanded, “O Moses! Make for us a god like their gods.” He replied, “Indeed, you are a people acting ignorantly!

commentary.text: This shows us the height of ingratitude even after they were rescued by Allah SWT from Pharaoh.

Even though the Israelites had been taught and trained by Musa (PBUH) for forty Years and by Joshua for twenty-eight years, they had still been unable to purge their minds of those influences which had warped their outlook and mentality during their period of bondage under Pharaoh. These Muslims had begun to look upon idol-worship as natural. Even after their exodus, the sight of a temple would incline them to indulge in the idolatrous practices which they had observed among their former masters.

translation.text: And ˹remember˺ when We rescued you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with dreadful torment—killing your sons and keeping your women. That was a severe test from your Lord.

commentary.text: Musa (PBUH) reminded the Children of Israel of Allah's blessings, such as saving them from Pharaoh’s tyranny and the humiliation as well as the disgrace they suffered. He reminded them of the glory and revenge against their enemy, when they watched them suffering in disgrace, destroyed by drowning and meeting utter demise.

sections.title: 142-144 Musa (PBUH)'s communication with Allah

translation.text: We appointed for Moses thirty nights then added another ten—completing his Lord’s term of forty nights. Moses commanded his brother Aaron, “Take my place among my people, do what is right, and do not follow the way of the corruptors.”

commentary.text: After the exodus of the Israelites from Egypt which marks, on the one hand, the end of the constraints of slavery and on the other, the beginning of their life as an independent nation, Musa (PBUH) was summoned by God to Mount Sinai in order that he might receive the Law for Israel (Torah). He was initially summoned for a period of thirty days so that he might single-mindedly devote himself to worshipping, fasting, meditation, reflection and thus develop the ability to receive the revelation which was to put a very heavy burden upon him.
Musa (PBUH)’s brother Aaron was put in charge.

translation.text: He said, ‘Moses, I have raised you above other people by [giving you] My messages and speaking to you: hold on to what I have given you; be one of those who give thanks.’

commentary.text: Allah SWT states that He spoke to Musa (PBUH) directly and informed him that He has chosen him above the people of his time, by His Message and by speaking to him.

sections.title: 145-147 Musa (PBUH) was given the written tablets of Taurat (Torah) and Arrogant people cannot get guidance

translation.text: We wrote for him on the Tablets ˹the fundamentals˺ of everything; commandments and explanations of all things. ˹We commanded,˺ “Hold to this firmly and ask your people to take the best of it. I will soon show ˹all of˺ you the home of the rebellious.

commentary.text: The Bible categorically mentions that the tablets were of stone. The Israelites were asked to hold fast to the Law and follow its plain meaning, a meaning which can be grasped by an ordinary man of sound heart and good intent. Basic warnings/alerts were mentioned so that man can remain within prescribed boundaries and then use his/her freedom of choice in life.

translation.text: I will turn away from My signs those who act unjustly with arrogance in the land. And even if they were to see every sign, they still would not believe in them. If they see the Right Path, they will not take it. But if they see a crooked path, they will follow it. This is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.

commentary.text: Arrogance is a thing most hated by Allah SWT.

sections.title: 148-151 Israelites started worshipping calf after witnessing their miraculous deliverance

translation.text: In the absence of Moses, his people made from their ˹golden˺ jewelry an idol of a calf that made a lowing sound. Did they not see that it could neither speak to them nor guide them to the ˹Right˺ Path? Still they took it as a god and were wrongdoers.

commentary.text: Also see Surah 2 Ayat 93

Their cow-worship was another manifestation of the Israelites' slavish attachment to the Egyptian traditions at the time of the Exodus. What is more surprising about their turn to idolatry is that it took place just three months after their escape from Egypt. During that time, they had witnessed the parting of the sea, the drowning of Pharaoh, and their own deliverance from what otherwise seemed inescapable slavery, to the Egyptians. They knew well that all those events had taken place owing to the unmistakable and direct interference of the all-powerful God. Yet they had the audacity to demand that their Prophet should make for them a false god that they might worship.
Soon after Musa (PBUH) left them for Mount Sinai, they themselves contrived a false god.

translation.text: And when Moses returned to his people, full of wrath and sorrow, he said: ''Vile is the course you have followed in my absence. Could you not patiently wait for the decree of your Lord?'' And he threw down the Tablets [of the Law] and took hold of his brother's head, dragging him to himself. Aaron said: ''My mother's son, the people overpowered me and almost killed me. So let not my enemies gloat over me, and do not number me among the wrong-doing folk.''

commentary.text: Upon his return Musa (PBUH) was sad, infuriated and disappointed when he saw the false god. He threw down the tablets and got hold of his brother’s head.
Later he calmed down and asked for forgiveness.

sections.title: 152-156 Worshippers of the calf incurred the wrath of Allah

translation.text: Those who worshipped the calf will certainly be afflicted with Allah’s wrath as well as disgrace in the life of this world. This is how We reward those who invent falsehood.

commentary.text: Punishment in this world and the next.
Those who invent lies against Allah SWT and commit shirk.

sections.title: 157 Advent of Prophet Muhammad was described in Torah and Gospel

translation.text: “˹They are˺ the ones who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whose description they find in their Torah and the Gospel. He commands them to do good and forbids them from evil, permits for them what is lawful and forbids to them what is impure, and relieves them from their burdens and the shackles that bound them. ˹Only˺ those who believe in him, honour and support him, and follow the light sent down to him will be successful.”

commentary.text: Formula for Success
Tauhid + Belief in His Messenger

sections.title: 158 Muhammad (pbuh) is the Prophet for the whole of mankind

translation.text: Say [Muhammad], ‘People, I am the Messenger of God to you all, from Him who has control over the heavens and the earth. There is no God but Him; He gives life and death, so believe in God and His Messenger, the unlettered prophet who believes in God and His words, and follow him so that you may find guidance.’

commentary.text: Prophet Muhammad for entire mankind – not a particular nation as previous Prophets.

sections.title: 159-162 Allah provided food and water in the desert to the people of Musa (PBUH)

translation.text: We divided them into twelve tribes—each as a community. And We revealed to Moses, when his people asked for water, “Strike the rock with your staff.” Then twelve springs gushed out. Each tribe knew its drinking place. We shaded them with clouds and sent down to them manna and quails, ˹saying˺, “Eat from the good things We have provided for you.” They ˹certainly˺ did not wrong Us, but wronged themselves.

commentary.text: Twelve large families that became nations or tribes (sons of Yaqub). Water and food provided by Allah SWT was distributed in an organized.

translation.text: And ˹remember˺ when it was said to them, “Enter this city ˹of Jerusalem˺ and eat from wherever you please. Say, ‘Absolve us,’ and enter the gate with humility. We will forgive your sins, ˹and˺ We will multiply the reward for the good-doers.”

commentary.text: Jerusalem or Jericho was the town they were told to enter it with humility asking for forgiveness of their sins.

translation.text: The wrongdoers among them substituted another saying for that which had been given them, so We sent them a punishment from heaven for their wrongdoing.

commentary.text: Also see Surah Baqarah Ayat 58 -9 and 74-5

sections.title: 163-168 Jewish Sabbath, the violation, and Allah's scourge

translation.text: [Prophet], ask them about the town by the sea; how its people broke the Sabbath when their fish surfaced for them only on that day, never on weekdays– We tested them in this way: because of their disobedience–

commentary.text: The Jews transgress the Sanctity of the Sabbath

‘Sabbath', which means Saturday, was declared a holy day of the week for the Israelites whereby they were required to strictly keep the Sabbath which meant that they may not engage in any worldly activity; they may not cook, nor make their slaves or cattle serve them.

The village mentioned here is Aylah, on the shore of the Red Sea. On the day of the Sabbath, the fish would swim openly and close to the surface of the water but the villagers were prohibited to fish due to the Sabbath. Then the fish would hide for the rest of the week. This was a test from Allah SWT.

The villagers decided to lay fishing nets out on Friday and then pulled all the fish out on Sunday. 
By using this deceitful trick to violate Allah's prohibitions they took an action that seemed legal on the surface but in reality, transgressed the prohibition.

Men are tested by God in a variety of ways. When a person or group of people begin to turn away from God and incline themselves towards disobedience, then God provides abundant opportunities for them to disobey. This is done in order that the full potential for disobedience, which had remained hidden because of lack of such an opportunity, might come to the surface.

translation.text: When they ignored the warning they were given, We rescued those who used to warn against evil and overtook the wrongdoers with a dreadful punishment for their rebelliousness.
But when they stubbornly persisted in violation, We said to them, “Be disgraced apes!”

commentary.text: Also see Surah Baqarah Ayat 65
The whole community that tried to trick Allah SWT was transformed into monkeys/apes. Even in that state they could recognize each other and then died after three days.
Lesson: Punishment fits the crime. The tried to deceive Allah SWT so Allah SWT tricked them.

sections.title: 169-171 Jews' wrong belief about Allah's forgiveness

translation.text: Then others succeeded them who inherited the scriptures, and yet kept themselves occupied in acquiring the goods of this world and kept saying: ''We shall be forgiven.'' And when there comes to them an opportunity for acquiring more of those goods, they seize it. Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them that they would not ascribe to Allah anything but the truth? And they have read what is in the Book and know that the abode of the Hereafter is better for the God-fearing. Do you not understand?

commentary.text: Previous Ayat’s talking about early generations of BI. But their successors were bad substitutes. Then another generation came (religious scholars) who inherited the Torah but their focus was worldly prosperity. Financial gain for legal and religious rulings. They altered the scriptures so as to please/accommodate their audience. They take such bold steps with the full confidence that they will be spared by Allah SWT due to their lineage – the Chosen People of the Lord. This Ayat is mostly regarding religious scholars and judges.
Hadith: Whoever strives for this world then his afterlife will suffer. Whoever strives for the afterlife his next world will suffer.

sections.title: 172-174 Mankind's testimony that Allah is their Rabb at the time of Adam's creation

intro.text: For the next three rukus we will discover some key Islamic philosophies/wisdom being mentioned:
First is our covenant with Allah SWT (Ayat 172)
Second is the battle between our higher self or fitra with our baser worldly desires (Ayat 175)
Third is those humans without guidance are no better than cattle or animals. (Ayat 179)

translation.text: [Prophet], when your Lord took out the offspring from the loins of the Children of Adam and made them bear witness about themselves, He said, ‘Am I not your Lord?’ and they replied, ‘Yes, we bear witness.’ So you cannot say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘We were not aware of this,’

commentary.text: This event took place in Alam ul Arwah, at the time of the creation of Adam.  When God gathered all human beings, divided them into different groups, granted them human form, the faculty of speech and made them enter into a covenant.
He asked them: 'Am I not your Lord?' They (we) replied: 'Assuredly you are Our Lord.'

Then God told them: 'I call upon the sky and the earth and your own ancestor, Adam, to be witness against you lest you should say on the Day of Judgement that you were ignorant of this. Know well that no one other than Me deserves to be worshipped and no one other than Me is your Lord. So do not ascribe any partner to Me. I shall send to you My Messengers who will remind you of this covenant which you made with Me. I shall send down to you, My Books.' In reply all said: ' Yes, we bear witness that You are Our Lord and our Deity. We have no lord or deity other than You.'

This event has also been interpreted by some commentators in a purely allegorical sense. They are of the opinion that the purpose of the Quran is merely to emphasize that the acceptance of God's lordship is innate in human nature. However, this was narrated in such a way as to suggest that the event did actually take place.
Thus, now there is no excuse to say that we did not know or we are only following our assertors. (Explanation by Maulana Maududi)
Lesson: This is why all humans seek a purpose or meaning of life.  This is our fitra or innate pre-disposition of submission to Allah SWT and a need for good.

sections.title: 175-178 Example of those who deny Allah's revelations

translation.text: [Prophet], tell them the story of the man to whom We gave Our messages: he sloughed them off, so Satan took him as his follower and he went astray

commentary.text:
Story Bal`am bin Ba`ura
This Ayat is about Bal`am bin Ba`ura' a scholar from the Children of Israel, whom Allah SWT had given the knowledge of His Ayat (guidance). But he leaves the Quran for the world and thus Satan gets hold of him.
Lesson: Relate this Ayat to ourselves. Quran is our protection against Satan. The Quran should be our consistent companion throughout the up’s and down’s of life.

translation.text: If We had willed, We would have elevated him with Our signs, but he clung to this life—following his evil desires. His example is that of a dog: if you chase it away, it pants, and if you leave it, it ˹still˺ pants. This is the example of the people who deny Our signs. So narrate ˹to them˺ stories ˹of the past˺, so perhaps they will reflect.

commentary.text: The aspiration for worldly and base desires of this life overpowered this person when Allah SWT would have raised him to a very high status via His Ayat or Guidance.

He, however, overly occupied himself with the advantages, pleasures, and embellishments of the worldly life. Instead of resisting worldly temptations, he totally, succumbed to them so much so that he abandoned altogether his lofty spiritual ambitions and became indifferent to the possibilities of intellectual and moral growth. Satan continually led him from one act of depravity to another until he landed him in the company of those who are totally under Satan's control and who have lost all capacity for rational judgement.

This is followed by a statement in which God likens the person in question to a dog. A dog's protruding tongue and the unceasing flow of saliva from his mouth symbolize unquenchable greed. Similarly a man bent upon fulfilling his desires is never satisfied.
Lesson: Often what keeps us away from the Quran is our desires. So choose wisely.

sections.title: 179-181 Misguided people are like animals or even worse

translation.text: Indeed, We have destined many jinn and humans for Hell. They have hearts they do not understand with, eyes they do not see with, and ears they do not hear with. They are like cattle. In fact, they are even less guided! Such ˹people˺ are ˹entirely˺ heedless.

commentary.text: When man turns away from Iman and resorts to rebellion against Allah SWT, then his heart, hearing, seeing are all sealed or covered. They cannot accept the truth even if they tried. Thus, they are no longer thinking humans in the true sense they are just animals in fact even worse than them. Because mankind has been created at a high level for a greater purpose.
Lesson: Don’t be like cattle who are mindlessly following and just eat, sleep and die. Allah SWT has made the entire universe to serve us. We are the best of all creations.

translation.text: Allah has the Most Beautiful Names. So call upon Him by them, and keep away from those who abuse His Names. They will be punished for what they used to do.

commentary.text: Understand Allah SWT attributes via His names. The 'most excellent names' used of God express His greatness and paramountcy, holiness, purity, and the perfection and absoluteness of all His attributes. Call upon your Raab by His most beautiful names. Ya Karim, Ya Wali, Ya Allah, Ya Raabi.
And avoid/leave those who twist and deviate the names of Allah SWT.

sections.title: 182-188 Those who deny Allah's revelations are drawing closer to destruction and Prophet himself has no power to benefit anyone or to avert any harm

translation.text: As for those who deny Our signs, We will gradually draw them to destruction in ways they cannot comprehend.

commentary.text: Those who reject Allah SWT’s Ayat’s, then Allah SWT facilitates the path they desire. Slowly and gradually Allah SWT seizes them in ways they perceive not; meaning the doors of provisions will be opened for them. They will be deceived by all this and think that they are on the correct path.
Also see:  Ayat 6:44-45

So, when they forgot (the warning) with which they had been reminded, We opened for them the gates of every (pleasant) thing, until in the midst of their enjoyment in that which they were given, all of a sudden, We took them (in punishment), and lo! They were plunged into destruction with deep regrets and sorrow. So the root of the people who did wrong was cut off. And all the praises and thanks are to Allah, the Lord of all that exists.

Lesson: Ironically such people start becoming very successful in life but in reality, it is Allah SWT who is letting them sin as much as possible by giving them every opportunity/time to hang themselves (so to speak). Such people are deluded into thinking that Allah SWT must be very happy with them to provide such worldly gifts and position.
The term for this is “istagrar.”

translation.text: Say [Prophet], ‘I have no control over benefit or harm, [even] to myself, except as God may please: if I had knowledge of what is hidden, I would have abundant good things and no harm could touch me. I am no more than a bearer of warning, and good news to those who believe.’

commentary.text: Reason: “The people of Mecca said: ‘O Muhammad, does not your Lord inform you about lower prices before they go up, and thus you buy and make profit? And does He not inform you about the land which is about to suffer drought and, thus, you travel to a land which is more fertile?’ And so Allah SWT revealed this Ayat”.
Allah SWT commanded His Prophet to inform people about himself, that is, he does not know the unseen future rather he knows of what Allah informs him.

sections.title: 189-198 Allah created the whole of mankind from a single soul and Reality of those gods whom people worship beside Allah and Allah is the Protecting Friend of the righteous

translation.text: He is the One Who created you from a single soul, then from it made its spouse so he may find comfort in her. After he had been united with her, she carried a light burden that developed gradually. When it grew heavy, they prayed to Allah, their Lord, “If you grant us good offspring, we will certainly be grateful.”

commentary.text: Marriage is to find comfort and peace/sukoon as well as tranquility and happiness at home and in each other.
When a couple realizes, they are going to have a child they beseech Allah SWT to grant them a healthy off spring.
Lesson: Husbands particularly find peace and comfort in a wife. Women must understand this.

translation.text: And yet when He gives them a good child they ascribe some of what He has granted them to others. God is far above the partners they set up alongside Him!

commentary.text: Then when Allah SWT grants them a good, healthy righteous child the parents instead of thanking Allah SWT thank others i.e Doctors, idols they worshipped, Saints they prayed to etc.

translation.text: And if you ˹idolaters˺ call upon them for guidance, they cannot respond to you. It is all the same whether you call them or remain silent.

commentary.text: What is the extent of their power of these false gods set up by the polytheists? Not only do they not have the power to guide others or even to answer the call of their devotees. They don’t create they are in fact part of creation. It is the same whether you call them or not as there will be no response.
Allah SWT here is challenging people to think.

Lesson: Initially these idols were created in an attempt to visualize the deities or gods, such as, god of fertility etc. So their justification is that we realize that this is just stone so we are not worshipping stone rather this is just a representation of the actual god. front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name Al-Anfal (The Bounties) from the first Ayat. Anfal is derived from nafal or bonus/extra. After victory in war the war booty is extra or a bonus.

front_matter.label: The Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: It was revealed after the Battle of Badr, the first battle between Islam and kufr.

front_matter.label: Subject/Topic of Discussion
front_matter.text:
The Battle of Badr has been reviewed in this Surah. But let it be noted that in some respects this review is quite different from the reviews that are usually made by the worldly commanders after a great victory.
Instead of gloating over the victory, the moral weaknesses that had come to the surface in that expedition have been pointed out so that the Muslims should try their best to reform themselves.
It has been impressed upon them that the victory was due to the help of Allah rather than to their own valor and bravery so Muslims should learn to rely on Him and obey Allah and His Messenger alone.
Then the Surah addresses the mushriks, the hypocrites, the Jews and the prisoners of this war.
It also gives instructions in regard to the spoils of war.

front_matter.label: Background
front_matter.text:
Second Group of Surahs:
(i) Surah Anam and Aaraf = Makki pair and (ii)  Surah Al-Anaf and Taubabah =  Mediani pair.
The link between this Mediani pair with the Makki pair is that the first group of Surah’s was basically a charge sheet regarding all the offences of the Bani Israel and the Mushraqeen of Makka.
The second pair is then after a Prophet is sent and nation refuses to believe then punishment is sent. The Battle of Badr is the first installment of punishments for the Quraish. The second installment of punishment comes in Surah Taubah.
After migration/hijra to Madina for the first time Allah SWT allowed the raising of hands by Muslims.
First six months in Madina were used for consolidation and organization then next one and half years used for strategies to economically blockage the Mushriqeen of Makka. After two years in Madian was the Battle of Badr.
FYI -- There is no concept of peaceful co-existence in Islam. First is passive resistance and then is actual fighting for domination.
Here there was a dispute re: war booty after the first war the Muslims ever fought regarding distribution of booty.

sections.title: 1-20 COMMANDMENT RELATING TO THE SPOILS OF WAR (BOOTY) AND BATTLE OF BADR, A BATTLE BETWEEN TRUTH AND FALSEHOOD

translation.text: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ regarding the spoils of war. Say, “Their distribution is decided by Allah and His Messenger. So be mindful of Allah, settle your affairs, and obey Allah and His Messenger if you are ˹true˺ believers.”

commentary.text: The analysis or critique of the battle starts with disagreements among Muslims regarding sharing the spoils of war. As this was their first experience of fighting under the banner of Islam, the Muslim soldiers were unaware of the rules and regulations required on the battlefield and afterwards.
Before the advent of Islam, a soldier would take all that he could lay his hands on, resulting in conflicts among soldiers often turning victory into defeat.

By declaring that all the spoils of war belong to God and His Messenger, the Quran resolved the matter by making it obligatory on all soldiers to commit all the spoils of war to the custody of the commander, concealing not even something as trivial as a sewing needle.

Subsequently the Quran laid down an elaborate set of laws to distribute the spoils of war. According to it, one-fifth of the spoils is to be deposited in the public treasury for public welfare and to provide support for the poor, while four-fifths is to be distributed among the soldiers. Surah Al-Anfal Ayat 41. It thus put an end to the evils inherent in the old system.
Note: The main objective of war is victory subsequently any spoils or bounty of war are extra/bonus or nafl, thus, the name of the Surah Al-Anfal.

translation.text: The ˹true˺ believers are only those whose hearts tremble at the remembrance of Allah, whose faith increases when His revelations are recited to them, and who put their trust in their Lord.

commentary.text: Also see Ayat 74 the second last Ayat of this Surah. Thus, the second Ayat and the second last Ayat when compiled together provide a complete definition of a true believer.

(8:74) Those who believe and have migrated and strove in the way of Allah, and those who gave them refuge and help - it is they who are the true believers. Theirs shall be forgiveness and honorable sustenance.
Also see Surah Al-Hujurat Ayat 15

Def of Muslim is belief in the five pillars of Islam. Def of true believers or Momin entails two additional characteristics, (i) complete faith and Iman and (ii) actions for Islam (jihad with ourselves and our wealth).
A true believer is one whose hearts tremble at the remembrance of Allah SWT, and his faith only increases with knowledge and they put complete trust in Allah SWT. (Complete faith and Iman)

High rank near Allah SWT

translation.text: Similarly, when your Lord brought you ˹O Prophet˺ out of your home for a just cause, a group of believers was totally against it.
They disputed with you about the truth after it had been made clear, as if they were being driven to death with their eyes wide open.

commentary.text: Now begins the narration re: the Battle of Badr:

When the people in question were required to fight in the Battle of Badr, they were reluctant to do so for they feared death and destruction. (Hypocrites). They made excuses as to why the Battle is not a good idea despite Allah SWT’s command and surety of success.
God's promise was that the Muslims would be able to overcome whichever of the two parties they wished to attack - the trading caravan or the Quraysh army.
Thus, it became clear who truly believed (complete faith and Iman and then were ready to take action) as opposed to those who said one thing and did another.

translation.text: to firmly establish the truth and wipe out falsehood—even to the dismay of the wicked.

commentary.text: This gives some idea of the prevalent situation at the time. As we have said earlier (see above, p. 128), the march of the Quraysh towards Madina meant that only one of the two would survive in Arabia - either Islam or the entrenched system of Jahiliyah (Ignorance). Had the Muslims not taken up the challenge, the very survival of Islam would have been imperiled. But since the Muslims took the initiative and dealt a severe blow to the military strength of the Quraysh it became possible for Islam to consolidate itself and subsequently the forces of Ignorance suffered a succession of humiliating reverses.

translation.text: ˹Remember˺ when you cried out to your Lord for help, He answered, “I will reinforce you with a thousand angels—followed by many others.”

commentary.text: Muslims invoke Allah’s help and Allah sends the Angels to help Them.
Allah SWT supported His Prophet and the believers with a thousand angels, five hundred under the leadership of Jibril on one side and five hundred under the leadership of Mikail.
Don’t beg people rather ask Allah SWT. Allah SWT sends help to those who go out in the path of Allah SWT – Definitely Allah SWT help and support in ways that you cannot even imagine.
Angles descended to defend and support the Muslims.

translation.text: Believers, when you meet the disbelievers in battle, never turn your backs on them:

commentary.text: Fleeing from Battle is prohibited – cannot flee the battlefield.

translation.text: If anyone does so on such a day– unless maneuvering to fight or to join a fighting group– he incurs the wrath of God, and Hell will be his home, a wretched destination!

commentary.text: Fleeing from Battle is prohibited unless it is a strategic/tactical move or orderly retreat.
Punishment for turning away from the battle field is a major sin that incurs the wrath of Allah SWT.

sections.title: 20-28 WORST PEOPLE IN THE SIGHT OF ALLAH ARE THOSE WHO DO NOT USE THEIR COMMON SENSE AND GUARD YOURSELVES AGAINST TEMPTATIONS OF SHAITAN

translation.text: Do not be like those who say, “We hear,” but in fact they are not listening.
The worst creatures in God’s eyes are those who are [willfully] deaf and dumb, who do not reason.

commentary.text: These above Ayat’s are for the hypocrites who were reluctant to go to war.

translation.text: And know that your wealth and your children are only a test and that with Allah is a great reward.

commentary.text: And know that your possessions and your children are but a trial and with Allah SWT lies true reward. So don’t pin your hopes and aspirations on wealth and children rather have complete trust and faith in Allah SWT.

Excessive love of money and one's children often impair the sincerity of a person's faith and often lead man to hypocrisy, treachery and dishonesty. The Qur'an, therefore, clearly points out that since 1ove of wealth or children drives people off the right path, it constitutes a considerable test for them. One's property, one's business and one's offspring constitute a test for man since they have been in his custody so as to judge to what extent he observes the limits of propriety laid down by God and adequately performs his responsibilities. What is tested is how far man is able to control his animal self - which is strongly attached to worldly purposes - so that he is able to act as God's servant and render all the rights of worldly life in the manner laid down by God.

sections.title: 29-37 IF YOU BECOME GODFEARING, ALLAH WILL GRANT YOU WISDOM TO JUDGE BETWEEN RIGHT AND WRONG AND LAWFUL GUARDIANS OF KA'BAH ARE THOSE WHO HAVE FEAR OF ALLAH

translation.text: O believers! If you are mindful of Allah, He will grant you a standard ˹to distinguish between right and wrong˺, absolve you of your sins, and forgive you. And Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty.

commentary.text: Fear Allah SWT (have tawaqul) and then Allah SWT will show you the criteria for right and wrong. Making the right decisions at the right time.

If a man is God-fearing and tries his best to refrain from acts which displease God, God will create in him the ability to discern for himself which actions are proper and which are not; which attitude conduces to God's good pleasure and which is likely to incur His wrath. This inner light will serve as a pointer; guiding him as to when he should proceed and when he should refrain, telling him which is the path of truth and leads to God, and which is false and leads to Satan.

translation.text: And why should Allah not punish them while they hinder pilgrims from the Sacred Mosque, claiming to be its rightful guardians? None has the right to guardianship except those mindful ˹of Allah˺, but most pagans do not know.

commentary.text: It is not for the polytheists, to maintain the Masjids of Allah, while they witness disbelief against themselves. The works of such are in vain and in the Fire shall they abide.
Also see (9:17-18)
The Masjids of Allah shall be maintained only by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day; perform the Salah, and give the Zakah and fear none but Allah. It is they who are on true guidance.
Also see (2:217)

But a greater (transgression) with Allah is to prevent mankind from following the way of Allah, to disbelieve in Him, to prevent access to Al-Masjid Al-Haram (at Makkah), and to drive out its inhabitants,

sections.title: 38-40 UNBELIEVERS, WHO EMBRACE ISLAM, THEIR PAST IS FORGIVEN

translation.text: Say to those who have disbelieved [that] if they cease, what has previously occurred will be forgiven for them. But if they return [to hostility] - then the precedent of the former [rebellious] peoples has already taken place.

commentary.text: Encouraging the Disbelievers to seek Allah's Forgiveness, warning Them against Disbelief

Those who embrace Islam and repent then all their past sins and errors will be forgiven – clean slate. But if they repeat their hostility and return to kufur and disbelief then punishment will be the same as past nations.

translation.text: Fight against them until there is no more persecution—and ˹your˺ devotion will be entirely to Allah. But if they desist, then surely Allah is All-Seeing of what they do.

commentary.text: Also see Surah Al Baqarah Ayat 193

This is a repetition of the resolve, mentioned earlier in al-Baqarah 2: 193, for which Muslims are required to wage war. So as to establish a state of affairs wherein all obedience is rendered to Allah SWT alone. This alone is the purpose for which believers may, rather should, fight. Fighting for any other purpose is not lawful.
